solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vehicle producing poison, converting oxygen to a tar

indicators.note: converting one thing to another says one letter of the word is swapped for a new one

parts.note: something that produces poison is toxic
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a tar is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the crossword's other sailor

explanation.surface: A grumble about a car whose exhaust is toxic, as if the engine turned oxygen into tar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converting oxygen to a' swaps the O in TOXIC for A, giving TAXIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxicab is a hired car, so it is a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Old bear craving attention, taking its termination to heart

parts.note: to hack something is to bear or cope with it, as in 'can't hack it'

indicators.note: the word's last letter is moved from its end into its middle, its heart

parts.note: someone craving attention is needy

explanation.surface: An elderly bear sulks for attention and takes its ending to heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bear' reads as one creature, but 'Old' alone is the definition; 'taking its termination to heart' shifts the final letter of the needy word into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed means stale or overused, which is a figurative way of being old.

clue.text: Angry lecturer cycles off course

indicators.note: cycles says letters go round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: someone who lectures angrily is a ranter

explanation.surface: A furious lecturer pedals away from the planned route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycles' moves the final ER of RANTER round to the front, giving ERRANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying from the proper path, so wandering off course.

clue.text: Complete studies diminished twin within framework

indicators.note: within says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a grate is a framework of metal bars

indicators.note: diminished says the word is cut down, losing its final letter

parts.note: twin in the sense of double is dual

explanation.surface: A medical note: someone finishes their studies about a vanishing twin found inside a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diminished' docks the twin word's last letter; 'within' places what is left inside the framework.
explanation.definitionFit: To graduate is to finish a course of study and receive a degree.

clue.text: E.g. Heaven's quoted, renewing call for ruler's divine protection

indicators.note: renewing the letters means remaking them in a new order

explanation.surface: Heaven is cited as an example while a prayer for a monarch's safety is renewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renewing' rearranges the letters of EGHEAVENSQUOTED.
explanation.definitionFit: The British national anthem asks the Almighty to save and protect the monarch.

clue.text: Boron in air supplements cool atmosphere

indicators.note: supplements says the air word is added into the middle of the word for cool

parts.note: cool in the slang sense of excellent is ace

indicators.note: in puts the element symbol inside the word for air

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing, a mien
B is the chemical symbol for boron

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: boron added to the air supplies a cool atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the boron symbol inside the air word, making MBIEN; 'supplements' then puts that into the middle of the cool word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambience is the mood or character of a place, its atmosphere.

clue.text: Campus against students' club

parts.note: a campus stands for a university, a uni
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: A campus protest against a student society.
explanation.walkthrough: A students' union is the club and social centre of a university.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is the society that runs student clubs and facilities at a university.

clue.text: Last of breakfast cereal turned into mush

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter
turned into says the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: The leftover breakfast cereal has gone soggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned into' rearranges the letters of the cereal; 'mush' is the figurative sense, cloying sentiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle figuratively means cloying sentimentality, as does mush.

clue.text: Barry Island in appearance changed to a fair

parts.note: Baz is a familiar short form of the name Barry

indicators.note: changed to says one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Barry Island, a Welsh seaside resort, has been made over into a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island in appearance changed to a' turns AIR into AAR. Barry Island is a seaside resort near Cardiff with a fairground.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is a sale of goods, much like a charity fair.

clue.text: Add voice track to record sleeve for Joyce, say

parts.note: to dub a film is to add a voice soundtrack
a liner is the sleeve of a record, as in liner notes

explanation.surface: A recording engineer adds a voice track to a record sleeve for someone called Joyce.
explanation.walkthrough: James Joyce was born in Dublin and wrote the stories Dubliners.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce was born in Dublin, so he is an example of a native of that city.

clue.text: Playing links, a cup — not the last for him?

definitions.text: Playing links, a cup — not the last for him?

indicators.note: playing says the letters are put into play in a new order
not the last says the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A golfer plays a links course, chasing a cup that won't be his last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the last' trims cup to CU; 'Playing' shuffles LINKS, A and CU. A links is a seaside golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Nicklaus, the record major winner, is a golfer who won cup after cup.

clue.text: Europe protecting one local church person without power

indicators.note: protecting says the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: EU is the European Union
in dialect 'un means one, as in 'a good 'un'

explanation.surface: Europe shelters a local church figure who has no influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' wraps the Europe abbreviation round the dialect word for one, giving EUNU.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated man lacks virility; figuratively the word means someone ineffectual and powerless.

clue.text: Congratulations on puzzle, a 10:1 ratio?

parts.note: a maze is a puzzle of paths
in Roman numerals L is 50 and V is 5, so L to V is ten to one

explanation.surface: Praise for solving a puzzle, with odds of ten to one.
explanation.walkthrough: The ratio is written as L TO V in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew phrase is used to offer good wishes and congratulations.

clue.text: Byzantine hen price code

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so the letters are tangled

explanation.surface: A tortuous system for pricing hens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Byzantine' rearranges the letters of HENPRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To encipher is to put a message into secret writing, a verb sense of code.

clue.text: Dad up to no good, scoffing (26) wild snappers?

parts.note: papa is a word for dad

indicators.note: up to says take the word only as far as the letters that follow, dropping them

parts.note: 26 refers to the answer at 26 across: razzing is American slang for scoffing or jeering

explanation.surface: Dad misbehaves, eating while wild photographers snap away.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed (26) points to the answer at 26 across, telling you to use that nation's slang. 'up to no good' keeps the letters that come before the no-good abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Paparazzi are freelance photographers who pursue celebrities aggressively, so they are wild snappers.

clue.text: Put on dress coats, cold and bitter

indicators.note: coats says the dress word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a sari is an Indian dress
to don clothing is to put it on
C is an abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Dressing up in coats against the cold and bitter weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coats' wraps the Indian garment round the put-on word, giving SARDONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonic means grimly mocking, close to bitter or cynical.

clue.text: Washington ace entering rough and ready

indicators.note: entering says these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: rough means harsh
Washington DC is the US capital
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A Washington star player enters the scene, rough and ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts DCA inside HARSH. 'Ready' is slang for money in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The readies or ready money is cash available to spend, as is actual cash.

clue.text: Believing God isn't great, He is misquoted selectively

indicators.note: selectively says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A slogan that God is great has been misquoted as saying He isn't.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is the conviction that no deity exists.

clue.text: Making deliveries short, finally tie rope to secure canvas

indicators.note: short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: in cricket a player making deliveries is bowling

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cricketer cuts short his bowling spell to tie a rope round the canvas covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims BOWLING to BOWLIN; 'finally' adds E from tie.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship a bowline is a line holding the edge of a sail, which is canvas.

clue.text: Praise energy for lead of strong woman carrying barrel

indicators.note: carrying says the altered word holds the barrel letters inside
for lead of says the energy letter replaces the word's first letter

parts.note: an Amazon is a strong, warlike woman of legend
E is the symbol for energy in physics
BL is an abbreviation for barrel

explanation.surface: Applauding the energy of a powerful woman lugging a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for lead of' swaps the warrior woman's first letter for energy, making EMAZON; 'carrying' puts the barrel abbreviation inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To emblazon is to celebrate or extol publicly, a literary sense of praise.

clue.text: Description of superstore dismissing good person in clerical job

indicators.note: dismissing says a letter is sent away from the phrase

parts.note: a superstore can be described as a big shop

explanation.surface: A big store sacks a good employee from an office job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' drops the G for good from BIGSHOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a senior member of the clergy, holding clerical office.

clue.text: Started to accept Liberal's defence

indicators.note: to accept says the first word takes the letter in

parts.note: to start, like a nervous horse, is to shy, so started is shied
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A political story: someone began to embrace the Liberal case for defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts L inside SHIED.
explanation.definitionFit: A shield is a protective barrier, a means of defence.

clue.text: Insufficient guts to join the action?

indicators.note: insufficient says the word falls short, missing its last letter

parts.note: entera is the plural of enteron, the gut or alimentary canal

explanation.surface: Someone without enough nerve wonders whether to get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insufficient' trims ENTERA to five letters. The definition plays on stage directions telling an actor to come on.
explanation.definitionFit: To come onto stage is to join the action of a play, as a stage direction instructs.

clue.text: Dodgy duke removed from Bedfordshire town

indicators.note: removed from says a letter is taken out of the town's name

parts.note: Dunstable is a town in Bedfordshire, an English county north of London

explanation.surface: A shady aristocrat has been expelled from a Bedfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is a county north of London; 'removed from' takes the D out of DUNSTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstable means unsound or unreliable, which is what dodgy describes.

clue.text: Forbear having 50 per cent cut on prime minister's low pay

indicators.note: on says the halved word comes after the prime minister

parts.note: William Pitt, Elder and Younger, were British prime ministers

indicators.note: having fifty per cent cut keeps only the first half of the word

parts.note: a forbear (forebear) is an ancestor

explanation.surface: An ancestor complains of a prime minister's pay cut of half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having 50 per cent cut' halves ANCESTOR to ANCE, which goes 'on' PITT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a tiny, inadequate wage.

clue.text: Start off bender with a leak?

indicators.note: start off says the first letter is removed

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree, a bout of boozing

explanation.surface: Beginning a drinking session that ends in a trip to relieve oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' drops the B of BOOZING. 'Leak' hints at a drinker's trip to the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oozing seeps slowly, as liquid escaping from a leak does.

clue.text: Idle, perhaps a bloke crosses from other side of herring pond?

definitions.text: from other side of herring pond

indicators.note: crosses says the man phrase goes across, around the name

parts.note: a bloke is a man
Eric Idle of Monty Python is an example of an Eric

explanation.surface: A lazy fellow crosses over the herring pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' looks like lazy but is Eric Idle of Monty Python. The herring pond is a jokey name for the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: The herring pond is the Atlantic, so someone from its far side, seen from Britain, comes from the USA.
